question: By selling an article for Rs. 820, Abhi loses 18%. To gain 25.5%, he should sell it for:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Loss = 18%

Required profit = 25.5%

The final selling price = 820 × (100/82) × (125.5/100)

= Rs. 1255

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price at 18% loss = Rs.820 

**Formulas used:**

Profit or Loss is calculated on Cost Price which is 100% of itself. 

Selling Price = Cost Price × (100 ± Proft/Loss)%

⇒ Cost Price = Selling Price/(100 ± Proft/Loss)%

**Calculation:**

Cost Price = 820/(100 - 18)%

⇒ Cost Price = Rs.1000

Selling Price at 25.5% profit = 1000 × (100 + 25.5)%

⇒ 1000 × 125.5/100 

⇒ Rs.1255

**∴ The required result is Rs.1255**
